radiology_report:
Ziekenhuis Gelderse Vallei (Ede)
Department of Radiology
Date: 15 January 2025
Exam: Multiparametric MRI prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA to 9.9 ng/mL. Previous biopsy negative. Request for lesion characterization and PI-RADS scoring.

FINDINGS: Prostate volume measures 50.0 mL. The transition zone demonstrates benign nodular enlargement without suspicious diffusion restriction. No suspicious focal lesion is identified. A small, non-suspicious area measuring 6 mm is located in the left posterolateral peripheral zone, showing mildly increased T2 signal and no appreciable restriction on diffusion-weighted imaging or enhancement on dynamic contrast sequences. The neurovascular bundles are symmetric and intact. No suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy or osseous lesions are visualized within the field of view.

IMPRESSION: Multiparametric MRI of the prostate demonstrates peripheral zone findings classified as PI-RADS 2. Prostate volume is 50.0 mL, yielding a PSA density of 0.19 ng/mL/mL. Clinical T stage is cT1c. csPCa predicted probability 0.6607788.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: Routine screening visit documented a prostate-specific antigen level of 3.1 ng/mL, which remained within age-adjusted reference ranges. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable, and the patient reported only mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS of 7. Given the stable biochemical profile and absence of clinical concerns, routine annual monitoring was scheduled.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: Follow-up consultation noted a repeat PSA of 2.5 ng/mL, showing a slight decrease from the previous measurement. The patient remained asymptomatic regarding urinary function, and no new comorbidities were reported. A systematic prostate biopsy was subsequently arranged to further evaluate baseline risk, with tissue processing initiated at the time of this visit.

pathology_report:
Histological examination of the prostate tissue specimens obtained via transrectal ultrasound-guided systematic biopsy reveals benign prostatic hyperplasia and focal chronic inflammation. No malignant glands are identified. The Gleason score is reported as 0+0, corresponding to ISUP grade group 0. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. Perineural invasion is absent. This represents the initial biopsy performed to date, demonstrating a stable benign histological profile without evidence of carcinoma.
